scope: Vite 6.4.5 to 8.3.6, which builds with rolldown 1.2.16 (oxc, lightningcss) instead of Rollup and esbuild; what the frontend output contains afterwards and where it comes from. Not final application compliance or installer delivery.

configuration.build_target_reason: Vite 6's default ('modules', ESBUILD_MODULES_TARGET in vite 6.4.5 dist/node/constants.js). Vite 8 defaults to 'baseline-widely-available' (Safari 16), but the app supports macOS 11.
configuration.js_comments: build.rolldownOptions.output.comments.legal = true; Vite 8 sets legal: false when it minifies.
configuration.css_comments: Plugin aidevbridge:keep-css-license-comments: lightningcss keeps only a /*! comment at the start of a file, so CSS comments that name a copyright are collected in transform and put at the start of each CSS asset in generateBundle, opened with /*!.

after.source: node_modules/@rolldown/binding-win32-x64-msvc/rolldown-binding.win32-x64-msvc.node: rolldown's built-in viteModulePreloadPolyfillPlugin, which vite:modulepreload-polyfill in vite 8.3.6 dist/node/chunks/node.js calls

modulepreload_polyfill.same_program: The embedded JS is Vite's polyfill function: the same feature check, the same querySelectorAll and MutationObserver over link[rel=modulepreload] and the same fetch options; it differs in formatting and comments only.

source_package.readme_statement: Code copied from the published package `@babel/runtime`. All credits to the Babel team.

after.carrier: rolldown's native binding embeds the oxc runtime helpers (it names @oxc-project/runtime and carries Babel's '@babel/helpers - typeof' marker) and inlines the ones the transformed code needs; no runtime package is installed.

js.text: the six xterm.js @license MIT headers, as before

decision: npm:vite stays included for the polyfill (Vite's code, Vite core MIT text). npm:rolldown is included: its native library carries and emits the polyfill and the helpers (rolldown MIT text). frontend:oxc-runtime-helpers is included with the MIT texts of @babel/runtime and @oxc-project/runtime. npm:lightningcss (MPL-2.0) only minifies CSS and contributes no code: excluded. npm:esbuild and npm:rollup left the lock file and the output; their decisions and the esbuild text file leave the selection.
